device: 16-inch M1 Max class (T6001), Linux, Vulkan (honeykrisp), wheel 5b18306
method: pure per-op injection: identical CPU-recorded inputs fed to each op on both backends; bf16-faithful references; three-way rms_norm resolution with raw bits; ranked relL2 table

raw_first_divergence.classification: LOCAL 1-ulp bf16 difference: Vulkan single-round vs CPU/Metal two-round (Metal fused is BIT-IDENTICAL to CPU composite; raw bits at max element: fp32 -21.636024 -> device -21.625 [RNE-correct nearest] vs CPU/Metal -21.75 [one grid step farther])

finding: ALL quantized matmul ops carry 3.5-10.6% relL2 divergence (10-40x the 0.27% bf16-ulp class of conv/GDN/norm ops); moe_gather_qmm is the worst. Root cause of the layer trace growth (~6% layer-0 -> ~19% logits) is the quantMM kernel numerics (CPU quantized.cpp vs Vulkan qmm/gather_qmm shader accumulation/dequant), NOT rms_norm and NOT GDN.
claim_scope: per-op divergence localization; no qualification change; no tolerance proposal; no performance claim
